name: Ping
description: Ping is a network utility used to test the reachability of a host on an Internet Protocol (IP) network.

inputs.label: Target Host/IP:
inputs.help: The hostname or IP address to ping.

inputs.label: Packet Count (-c):
inputs.help: Number of packets to send. Leave blank for continuous ping.

inputs.label: Interface (-I):
inputs.help: Source interface to send packets from.

inputs.label: Interval (-i):
inputs.help: Wait a number of seconds between sending each packet.

inputs.label: Target List File (-i):
inputs.help: Read a list of targets from a file. Note: Not all `ping` implementations support this.

inputs.label: Upload Target List:
inputs.help: Upload a file containing a list of targets (one per line).

inputs.label: Quiet Output (-q)
inputs.help: Suppress all output except for the summary lines.

inputs.label: Flood Ping (-f)
inputs.help: Send packets as fast as possible. Useful for stress testing. Note: Requires root privileges and is highly intrusive.

inputs.label: Preload (-l):
inputs.help: Send a number of packets as fast as possible before switching to normal behavior.

inputs.label: TTL (-t):
inputs.help: Set the Time to Live for the packets.

inputs.label: Pattern (-p):
inputs.help: Fill the packets with up to 16 bytes of data from the given hex pattern.

inputs.label: TOS (-o):
inputs.help: Set the Type of Service/DSCP for the packets.

inputs.label: Use IPv6 (-6)
inputs.help: Use IPv6 packets instead of IPv4.

inputs.label: Beep on Success (-a)
inputs.help: Beep when a host is reachable.

inputs.label: Add Timestamp (-D)
inputs.help: Add a timestamp to each line.

inputs.label: Additional Arguments:
inputs.help: Any other ping arguments not covered by the GUI. Enter them exactly as you would on the command line.
